cases.description: When getEvaluationPath() returns a non‑null path and getSchemaNode() returns a non‑null JsonNode, toString() should concatenate them in the format "<path>" : <node>. A spy of JsonSchema is used to stub getEvaluationPath() to return "/properties/name" and getSchemaNode() to return a JsonNode whose toString() yields {"type":"string"}.

If getEvaluationPath() returns null, Java string concatenation converts it to the literal "null". The method should still produce a valid string without throwing. A spy is configured to return null for getEvaluationPath() and a normal JsonNode for getSchemaNode().

When getSchemaNode() returns null, the call to getSchemaNode().toString() triggers a NullPointerException. The test verifies that the exception is thrown. A spy is configured to return a non‑null path and null for getSchemaNode().
When both getEvaluationPath() and getSchemaNode() return null, the method attempts to invoke toString() on the null schema node, which results in a NullPointerException.
When getEvaluationPath() returns an empty string and getSchemaNode() returns a JsonNode representing {"type":"boolean"}, toString() should produce a string with empty quotes before the colon.
When getEvaluationPath() returns a string consisting solely of whitespace characters, those spaces must be preserved inside the quotes in the resulting string.
When getEvaluationPath() contains spaces (or other printable characters), they should appear unchanged in the output, demonstrating that the method does not trim or alter the path.
When getSchemaNode() is an array node containing multiple element schemas, its toString() representation (a JSON array) must be concatenated correctly with the evaluation path.

group: JsonSchema.toString - repeated calls produce equal strings

cases.description: Calling toString() multiple times on the same JsonSchema instance should return equal string values each time (the content must be identical, even if the object reference differs).

group: JsonSchema.toString - schema node toString throws exception

cases.description: When getSchemaNode() returns a JsonNode whose toString() method throws an unchecked exception (e.g., IllegalStateException), the toString() implementation of JsonSchema propagates that exception. The test uses a spy or mock of JsonSchema that returns a valid evaluation path and a mocked JsonNode whose toString() is stubbed to throw IllegalStateException.
